eslint-setup.description: Set up proper ESLint configuration for all packages in the monorepo. Currently all packages have placeholder lint scripts ('echo Lint skipped...'). Create a root-level ESLint 9 flat config (eslint.config.js) with TypeScript support, React rules for apps/web, and appropriate ignores. Remove the legacy .eslintrc.json from apps/web and update all package lint scripts to run actual linting.
stepsToVerify: Run 'npm run lint' at root - should execute actual linting, not echo placeholder
Run 'npm run lint --filter=@invoice-generator/web' - should lint the web app
Run 'npm run lint --filter=@invoice-generator/pdf-generator' - should lint the pdf package
Run 'npm run lint --filter=@invoice-generator/shared-types' - should lint the shared types
Verify apps/web/.eslintrc.json no longer exists
Verify /eslint.config.js exists with ESLint 9 flat config format
Verify TypeScript files are linted (introduce a deliberate error and confirm it's caught)

minheight-persistence-fix.description: MinHeight properties (minHeightMode, minHeightValue, minHeightPercent) and showWhenEmpty are not persisted when saving/loading templates. Root cause: The Convex validators ARE correct, but the frontend code has TWO gaps: (1) StyleEditorHeader.tsx handleSave() explicitly picks properties but omits these 4 properties when sending to Convex, (2) template-store.ts setCurrentTemplateFromConvex() maps properties but omits these 4 when loading from Convex. Additionally, layoutConfig.grid is missing from the load mapping.
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor and load or create a template
Select 'Row Container' element and set Min Height to 'Fixed' with value 100
Select 'Work Hours Table' element and set Min Height to 'Percentage' with value 50
Save the template (ensure it syncs to Convex)
Hard refresh the page (Cmd+Shift+R)
Reload the same template from Convex
Verify Row Container still shows Min Height = Fixed, 100
Verify Work Hours Table still shows Min Height = Percentage, 50%
Test showWhenEmpty on a text element - toggle on, save, refresh, verify persistence

auto-hide-empty-elements.description: Empty text elements (where all token interpolations resolve to empty strings) should automatically hide in PDF output, not reserving any space. A 'Show when empty' property allows users to override this behavior per element.
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor and create/edit a template
Add a text element with content '{{billing_period}}'
Open Properties Panel - verify 'Show when empty' toggle exists for text elements
Go to Invoice page, ensure billing period fields are empty
Generate PDF - verify the billing_period text element does NOT appear (no blank space)
Return to Style Editor, enable 'Show when empty' for the text element
Generate PDF again - verify the element now reserves space (renders empty but occupies its position)

flex-items-presets.description: Replace the complex Flex Items section (Grow, Shrink, Basis numeric inputs) in Properties Panel with a simple dropdown of presets: 'Fixed Size' (element keeps defined size), 'Flexible' (grows and shrinks equally), 'Fill Available' (fills remaining space). Keep alignSelf as separate dropdown.
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor with a template containing a flex container (Row or Column)
Add or select a relative-positioned element inside the flex container
Verify the old 3-input Flex Items section (Grow/Shrink/Basis) is GONE
Verify new 'Flex Sizing' dropdown appears with options: Fixed Size, Flexible, Fill Available
Select 'Fixed Size' - element should maintain its defined dimensions
Select 'Fill Available' - element should expand to fill remaining container space
Select 'Flexible' - element should grow/shrink proportionally with siblings
Verify alignSelf dropdown still exists separately

auto-height-table-propagation.description: Work Hours Table (and other table elements) with auto height mode do not cause their parent Row/Column container to expand when the table has many rows. The layout engine's calculateAutoHeight() only handles layout_container children, ignoring tables. Fix: Pass invoice data to layout engine and estimate table heights based on actual content.
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor and create a template with a Row container set to heightMode='auto'
Add a Work Hours Table element inside the Row
Go to Invoice page and add 10+ work days with hours
Open Invoice Preview or generate PDF
Verify the Row container expands to fully contain the Work Hours Table
Verify table rows are NOT clipped or overflowing
Test with varying amounts of data (5, 10, 20 work days) - Row should adapt each time

min-height-property.description: Add minHeight property to all Style Editor elements with modes: None (no minimum), Fixed (specific value in points), Auto (content-based minimum), Percentage (of parent height). This allows users to set minimum height constraints on any element type.
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor and select any element type (text, table, divider, rectangle, logo, layout_container)
Verify 'Min Height' dropdown appears in Properties Panel with options: None, Fixed, Auto, Percent
Select 'Fixed' - verify number input appears, set value (e.g., 100)
Select 'Percentage' - verify percentage input with % suffix appears
Generate PDF - verify element respects the minimum height constraint
Test with element inside a container - percentage should be relative to parent height
Test with 'None' selected - element should use default behavior (no minimum enforced)
Test across all 8 element types to ensure consistent behavior

container-border-editor-only.description: Column Container and Row Container dashed borders (meant as editor-only visual indicators) incorrectly render in PDF output. The PDF renderer should not render dashed borders on layout containers since these are editor indicators, not intended for final output. Solid and dotted borders configured by users should still render normally.
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor and add a Column Container to a template
Verify the container shows a dashed blue border in the editor (visual indicator)
Generate PDF or open Invoice Preview
Verify the dashed border does NOT appear in the PDF output
In Style Editor, change the container's border style to 'solid'
Generate PDF again - verify the solid border now appears in PDF
Test with Row Container - same behavior expected (dashed hidden, solid visible)

empty-container-collapse.description: Empty layout containers (Row/Column) with showWhenEmpty=false and heightMode=auto still render with visible height (minimum 40 points) instead of collapsing to 0. Root cause: calculateAutoHeight() in layout-engine.ts returns minimum 40 for empty containers regardless of showWhenEmpty setting, and the PDF renderer doesn't check showWhenEmpty for layout containers (only for text elements).
stepsToVerify: Open Style Editor and add a Row Container to a template
Ensure the container has NO child elements inside it
Set the container's height mode to 'auto'
Verify 'Show when empty' is OFF (default for new containers)
Generate PDF or open Invoice Preview
Verify the empty container does NOT render at all (no visible height or space)
Toggle 'Show when empty' to ON for the container
Generate PDF again - verify the container now renders with minimum height
Add an element inside the container, generate PDF - verify container renders normally

unified-element-visibility-system.description: Create a future-proof Element Visibility System using a registry pattern. Problem: Layout engine calculates positions for all elements BEFORE the PDF renderer decides to hide them, causing gaps. Solution: Create a shared shouldRender() utility that both layout engine and PDF renderer use, with element-type-specific handlers. Architecture: (1) VisibilityHandler registry with default 'always render' fallback, (2) Custom handlers for: text (token interpolation + showWhenEmpty), tables (invoice data checks), logo (URL/invoice logo), containers (child visibility). (3) RenderContext for real invoices, PreviewRenderContext for editor. (4) registerHandler() API for runtime registration of new element types. New elements automatically work with default handler.
stepsToVerify: Verify new files exist: packages/shared-types/src/element-visibility/{index.ts, types.ts, registry.ts, utils.ts, handlers/*.ts}
Run 'npm run build' - all packages compile without errors
Run 'npm run test' - all visibility handler unit tests pass
Test text element: Create invoice with empty from_phone, add {{from_phone}} element - verify NO gap in PDF
Test text showWhenEmpty: Enable 'Show when empty' on text element - verify it renders even when empty
Test work hours table: Toggle showDetailedHours OFF - verify table gone AND no gap remains
Test line items table: Remove all line items - verify table gone AND no gap remains
Test logo: Remove all logo sources - verify logo element hidden AND no gap
Test container: Add container with single text child that resolves empty - verify container collapses
Test nested containers: Inner container empty causes outer to collapse if all children hidden
Test editor preview: Verify Style Editor preview matches PDF output behavior
Verify backwards compatibility: Existing templates load and render correctly without changes

element-visibility-future-proof-guide.description: Document the Element Visibility System for future element development. When adding a new element type: (1) Add type to templateElementTypeSchema in template.ts, (2) Decide if custom handler needed - NO handler needed if element always renders when visible, has no empty content, no invoice-data dependencies (default handler applies automatically), (3) If custom handler needed: create handler file in element-visibility/handlers/, export from handlers/index.ts, register in registry.ts VISIBILITY_HANDLERS object, (4) Add unit tests for the handler. Include code examples and decision flowchart.
stepsToVerify: Verify registry.ts contains comment block explaining when custom handlers are needed
Verify each handler file has JSDoc explaining the handler's rules
Test adding a hypothetical new element type without custom handler - verify it renders by default
Test registerHandler() API - verify runtime registration works
Verify code comments guide developers on extending the system
